results.result: HIF-Clear is a novel tissue-clearing method that uses 1% Tween 20 in citrate buffer with heating at 121°C for 10 min to achieve delipidation and antigen retrieval of centimeter-scale FFPE specimens.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C56, and C99 describe the core methodological innovation. The optimization experiments (C50-C55) demonstrate that 1% Tween 20 achieved superior delipidation and antigen retrieval compared to other detergents, with statistical significance (p=0.0035) and preservation of tissue integrity. CARS imaging (C62-C63) confirms lipid removal.

results.result: Among tested detergent conditions, only 1% Tween 20 achieved significant delipidation (p=0.0035) comparable to PFA-SDS (p=0.999) while maintaining tissue integrity and optimal antigen retrieval with high signal-to-background ratio.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C55 present systematic experimental comparison with statistical analysis (Figure 1A-C). The DiD quantification, immunolabeling quality assessment, and gross morphology evaluation provide converging evidence. Statistical tests are appropriate (one-way ANOVA with Tukey's test) with clear p-values reported.

results.result: HIF-Clear effectively removes myelinated lipids from FFPE mouse brains as confirmed by CARS imaging showing significantly lower signals compared to dewaxed FFPE controls.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C63 are supported by CARS spectroscopy data (Figure 1E-F) with quantification showing significant reduction in lipid signals. The technique is appropriate for detecting CH2 vibrations at 2850 cm⁻¹ characteristic of lipids. Statistical analysis confirms significance.

results.result: HIF-Clear enables whole-brain imaging of FFPE specimens with consistent dopaminergic neuron distributions matching Allen Brain Atlas, minimal distortion, and works on 15-year-old archived FFPE blocks at cellular resolution.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C68 demonstrate biological validation through anatomical consistency (Figure 2A-B), registration to reference atlas, volumetric comparison between hemispheres, and successful application to aged specimens (Figure 2C-E). The convergence of multiple validation approaches strengthens the conclusion.

results.result: HIF-Clear can be applied to long-term fixed specimens (3 months), though with reduced signal intensity and some regional signal loss, suggesting stronger antigen retrieval methods may be needed for optimization.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C70 and C134-C136 show HIF-Clear works on 3-month fixed specimens but with limitations (Figure 3). While major dopaminergic regions are labeled, pontine reticular nucleus loses signal and overall intensity is reduced. The speculation about stronger antigen retrieval (C136) indicates the method requires further optimization for long-term fixed samples.

results.result: HIF-Clear+ enables multi-round immunolabeling of centimeter-sized FFPE specimens through photobleaching and classical HIER, requiring overnight bleaching for <500 μm samples and ~72 hr for whole mouse brains, with preserved structural integrity and no cross-reactivity.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C78 describe the multi-round staining protocol with experimental validation (Figure 3—figure supplements 1-5). The requirement for post-fixation (C71), inability to strip antibodies with SDS (C72), and solution via photobleaching+HIER (C73-C74) are experimentally demonstrated. Timing parameters (C75-C76) and validation of integrity/specificity (C77-C78) are data-supported.

results.result: HIF-Clear+ successfully performed six-round immunolabeling for TH, TPH2, calbindin, PV, ChAT, and SMI312 on one intact FFPE mouse brain, revealing spatial distribution of neuronal markers including the Hbn-IPN circuitry involved in emotion, addiction, and reward.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C81 demonstrate the multiplexing capability with comprehensive imaging data (Figures 4-5). The six-round protocol with registration using lectin-labeled blood vessels as reference (C80) shows technical feasibility. The biological interpretation of Hbn-IPN circuitry (C81) is supported by citations to previous literature.

results.result: HIF-Clear+ can be applied to 1-mm-thick FFPE human brain specimens with three consecutive rounds of immunolabeling and homogeneous labeling throughout the entire depth.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C83 demonstrate human tissue compatibility with imaging at multiple depths (100, 500, 900 μm) showing consistent labeling (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1). This extends the method beyond mouse tissue and validates depth penetration in human samples.

results.result: FFPE-HIF-Clear reveals 3D cell distributions and spatial architecture in an astrocytoma model, showing nearly half of GFAP-positive astrocytes within the tumor with 63.9% located near the tumor surface (±200 μm).
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C86 demonstrate disease model application with 3D segmentation and spatial analysis (Figure 7A-F). The quantification of astrocyte-tumor distances provides specific numerical results with clear visualization of cell distributions, supporting the utility for disease microenvironment analysis.

results.result: HIF-Clear enables 3D quantification of therapeutic effects in TBI model, showing aNORO@sMN treatment rescued dopaminergic neuron ratio from 76% to 94% and increased blood vessel parameters (244% length, 301% surface area, 186% volume, 220% branches) compared to sham.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C91 demonstrate therapeutic evaluation with quantitative 3D analysis (Figure 7G-M). Multiple parameters (striatum volume, fiber tract volume, cell counts, vascular metrics) provide comprehensive assessment. Statistical analysis with n=3 and appropriate tests support the conclusions about treatment efficacy.

results.result: FFPE-HIF-Clear and SHIELD protocol with SDS-based electrophoresis yielded comparable quantitative outcomes in TBI model, indicating FFPE-HIF-Clear recovers biomarker signals as effectively as freshly processed samples.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C93 and C102 provide critical validation by comparing FFPE-HIF-Clear to fresh tissue processing (Figure 7—figure supplements 1-2). The comparable quantitative results across multiple parameters demonstrate that long-term FFPE storage does not compromise the ability to obtain meaningful biological data, validating the method's utility for archived specimens.

results.result: HIF-Clear-processed FFPE tissues can be directly expanded using original ProExM method without extended incubation, while ExPath cannot uniformly expand samples beyond 1 mm even with prolonged incubation.
results.evaluation: Claims C97-C98 demonstrate compatibility with expansion microscopy (Figure 8A-C). The comparison with ExPath shows HIF-Clear's advantage for thick specimens. Clear staining signals for SMI312 and MAP2 validate the approach, though the claim is limited to abundant targets.

results.result: FLASH and SDS-electrophoresis approaches showed weak TH signal, almost no NeuN signal, and strong nonspecific background noise in FFPE specimens, indicating insufficient antigen retrieval likely due to low-temperature experimental conditions.
results.evaluation: Claims C31-C37 establish the rationale for method development by demonstrating limitations of existing approaches (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a-b). The experimental comparison with multiple markers and the inference about temperature effects (C37) are supported by subsequent optimization showing improved results at 121°C.

results.result: Classical HIER at 121°C with citrate buffer alone resulted in weak signals, but adding 1% SDS significantly enhanced NeuN and SMI312 signals while causing tissue expansion and fragility.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C44 document the optimization process leading to the final protocol (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b). The observation of enhanced signals with SDS but tissue damage provides the rationale for testing alternative detergents, establishing the logical progression to the final Tween 20 protocol.

results.result: Dewaxing time should be increased for large samples to avoid opacity from residual wax, which can be eliminated through repeated dehydration/dewaxing without affecting tissue structure or antigenicity; complete dewaxing of whole mouse brain is achievable within 24 hr.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C61 provide practical guidance supported by experimental validation (Figure 1—figure supplements 3-4). The demonstration that repeated dewaxing maintains tissue integrity and antigenicity is important for method implementation, though these are methodological details rather than primary findings.

results.result: HIF-Clear enables centimeter-depth penetration of labeling agents in FFPE specimens, allows repeated staining without compromising integrity, and provides 3D histological information for accurate biomarker quantification and neuronal circuitry analysis.
results.evaluation: Claims C100-C101 and C106 summarize the key capabilities demonstrated throughout the manuscript. The centimeter-scale penetration is shown in multiple experiments (whole brain imaging, multi-round staining), and the utility for 3D analysis is validated in disease models. These are well-supported summary statements of demonstrated capabilities.

results.result: HIF-Clear works with both acidic (citrate buffer pH 6.0) and alkaline (Tris-EDTA pH 9.0) antigen retrieval solutions when supplemented with 1% Tween 20, facilitating antibody-specific optimization without compromising delipidation.
results.evaluation: Claims C124-C125 demonstrate flexibility of the method (Figure 8—figure supplement 1). Testing both pH conditions with satisfactory results shows the method is adaptable to different antibody requirements, which is important for practical implementation though not a primary finding.

results.result: HIF-Clear has limitations including testing limited to mouse and human brain under controlled conditions, potential variability with different fixation procedures, lack of extensive testing on non-brain tissues, sample size mostly 2-3 cm³, incompatibility with endogenous fluorescence, and uncertain compatibility with omics analysis.
results.evaluation: Claims C132-C143 provide honest assessment of method limitations. These are appropriately acknowledged scope limitations and areas requiring further investigation. The authors clearly distinguish between demonstrated capabilities and speculative applications, which is scientifically appropriate.

results.result: HIF-Clear could potentially enable creation of 3D biomarker atlases from archived specimens, facilitate deep learning model training, enable long-term preservation of mouse brains in FFPE blocks, minimize animal use in time-course studies, and catalyze broader investigations with further validation.
results.evaluation: Claims C107-C109, C111-C112, and C146 are speculative statements about potential future applications. While logically reasonable based on demonstrated capabilities, these represent proposed rather than demonstrated uses. The authors appropriately frame these as possibilities requiring further validation rather than established results.

results.result: HIF-Clear is a novel method using 1% Tween 20 in citrate buffer with heating at 121°C for 10 minutes to achieve delipidation and antigen retrieval in centimeter-thick FFPE specimens.
results.evaluation: All three reviewers affirm the method's effectiveness. The editor states the procedure is 'convincingly evaluated,' Reviewer 1 notes 'much improved with a more detailed methods description,' and Reviewer 2 emphasizes 'the simplicity and ease of implementation' and that 'evidence presented supports the effectiveness of the proposed method.'

results.result: 1% Tween 20 treatment achieved significant delipidation comparable to PFA-SDS controls, with the sharpest immunolabeling signals and confirmed removal of myelinated lipids by CARS imaging.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the delipidation data without challenge. Reviewer 2 notes 'direct comparisons with existing protocols' as a strength, and the editor confirms the method is 'convincingly evaluated.' No concerns are raised about the lipid removal claims or CARS validation.

results.result: HIF-Clear successfully labeled dopaminergic neurons in whole FFPE mouse brains with consistent anatomical distributions, minimal distortion, and worked on 15-year-old archived specimens.
results.evaluation: The reviewers affirm applicability to archival specimens. The editor states the method's 'applicability to further such samples is analyzed,' and Reviewer 2 notes the method 'holds promise for advancing tissue and 3D-specific determination of proteins.' No concerns are raised about the 15-year-old specimen data.

results.result: HIF-Clear+ enables multi-round immunolabeling using photobleaching and classical HIER, demonstrated through six-round labeling of different neuronal markers (TH, TPH2, calbindin, PV, ChAT, SMI312) in whole FFPE mouse brains.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm the multi-round capability. Reviewer 1 states 'They have also demonstrated the potential of multi-round immunolabelling using photobleaching,' and the editor confirms the method 'facilitating repeated rounds of immunolabeling.' The six-round demonstration is accepted without challenge.

results.result: HIF-Clear+ was successfully applied to 1-mm-thick human brain FFPE specimens with labeling homogeneity confirmed at depths of 100, 500, and 900 μm.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 raises concerns about the human tissue data, stating 'it is misleading to mention that the "fluorescent signals are comparable at varying depth" as the figure clearly showed a lack of continuous staining especially for SMI312 at 900um depth, and human brain tissue showed considerably increased background signal.' This challenges the claim of homogeneous labeling.

results.result: HIF-Clear enables 3D quantification for disease evaluation, demonstrated in astrocytoma and TBI models showing spatial cell distributions, therapeutic rescue of dopaminergic neurons, and enhanced angiogenesis.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the disease model applications. Reviewer 1 notes the method 'was useful for the study of disease models such as in an astrocytoma model' and 'in a traumatic brain injury model to quantify changes.' The editor confirms the method is 'convincingly evaluated' on archival pathology specimens.

results.result: HIF-Clear supports expansion microscopy, with FFPE tissues processed through HIF-Clear being directly expandable using ProExM without extended incubation.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 acknowledges 'They have also demonstrated...expansion microscopy with FFPE samples using Hif Clear.' The expansion microscopy compatibility is accepted without specific critique, though no detailed evaluation of the expansion data is provided.

results.result: The 1% Tween 20 condition retained good tissue integrity without apparent changes in size or color, unlike SDS which caused tissue expansion and fragility.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 raises a concern stating 'Some procedures, including the basic HIF-Clear protocol, seem to produce marked tissue expansion that is not mentioned in the manuscript. Users should take this fact into consideration when making measurements.' This directly contradicts the claim about retained tissue integrity.

results.result: FFPE-HIF-Clear and SHIELD protocol with SDS-based electrophoresis yielded comparable quantitative outcomes, indicating FFPE-HIF-Clear recovers biomarker signals as effectively as freshly processed samples.
results.evaluation: The comparison with fresh tissue methods is accepted by reviewers. Reviewer 2 notes 'Direct comparisons with existing protocols' as a major strength, and the comparable outcomes are not challenged in the reviews.

results.result: Long-term fixed specimens (3 months) exhibited reduced TH intensity and signal-to-noise ratio, with some regions losing signals, though HIF-Clear still has potential for such specimens.
results.evaluation: The limitations with long-term fixation are acknowledged in the manuscript and not challenged by reviewers. The authors' own data showing reduced signal quality is presented transparently, and reviewers do not dispute these findings.

results.result: HIF-Clear can be quickly and easily executed in pathology departments using standard procedures, making it readily applicable in clinical settings.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly affirms this, stating 'The simplicity and ease of implementation of the proposed procedure using common laboratory reagents distinguish it favorably' and 'the equipment and chemicals needed are broadly accessible.' The clinical applicability is a recognized strength.

comparisons.comparison: Perfect agreement on core methodological claims (C3, C56, C99). Both evaluations find the HIF-Clear method convincingly demonstrated and supported by evidence. OpenEval emphasizes statistical validation while peer reviewers highlight simplicity and implementation ease.

Complete agreement on biological validation claims (C65-C68). Both evaluations support the method's applicability to archival specimens including 15-year-old samples. OpenEval details anatomical consistency and atlas registration while peer reviewers affirm archival specimen utility.

Disagreement on human tissue compatibility (C82, C83). OpenEval finds claims supported with consistent labeling at multiple depths. Peer Reviewer 1 challenges this, noting discontinuous staining at 900μm depth and increased background signal, finding the claim misleading.

Agreement on FFPE-fresh tissue comparison (C92, C93, C102). Both evaluations support that FFPE processing yields comparable results to fresh tissue methods. Peer reviewers note direct protocol comparisons as a strength.

Agreement on long-term fixation limitations (C69, C70, C134, C135). Both evaluations acknowledge reduced signal quality and loss of labeling in some regions for 3-month fixed specimens. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN while peer reviewers accept the transparent presentation of limitations.

Agreement on disease model applications (C88-C91 overlap with C5, C85, C86). Both evaluations support the therapeutic evaluation and quantitative 3D analysis capabilities demonstrated in astrocytoma and TBI models.

Agreement on CARS lipid removal validation (C62, C63). Both evaluations support the delipidation claims. OpenEval details statistical significance of lipid signal reduction while peer reviewers accept the data without challenge.

Partial overlap on detergent optimization (C50-C52). Both support the systematic comparison showing Tween 20 superiority. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor while peer reviewers note direct protocol comparisons as a strength.

Agreement on multi-round staining capability (C79, C80, with C74 overlap). Both evaluations support the multiplexing demonstration. OpenEval details the six-round protocol with lectin-based registration while peer reviewers affirm photobleaching-based multi-round potential.

Agreement on astrocytoma model application (C85, C86). Both evaluations support the 3D segmentation and spatial analysis of tumor microenvironment. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative assessment while peer reviewers affirm disease model utility.

Agreement on expansion microscopy compatibility (C97, C98, with C6 overlap). Both evaluations support the demonstration though OpenEval notes limitation to abundant targets. Peer Reviewer 1 acknowledges the capability without detailed critique.

Potential disagreement on tissue integrity (C55). OpenEval supports claim of preserved gross morphology. Peer Reviewer 1 raises concern about 'marked tissue expansion' not mentioned in manuscript, suggesting integrity may be compromised.

Related to optimization process (C44). OpenEval supports the rationale for testing alternative detergents after observing SDS-induced tissue damage. Peer Reviewer 1's concern about tissue expansion may relate to this optimization pathway.

Minimal overlap on multi-round protocol details (C74). OpenEval supports photobleaching+HIER solution for antibody removal. Peer reviewers affirm multi-round capability more generally without detailed protocol evaluation.

OpenEval evaluates limitation acknowledgments (C132, C133, C137-C140, C142, C143) as appropriately transparent. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these limitation statements.
